Article Title: India needs heritage zones, not heritage islands
Article Text:
Advantages

Higher footfalls in the heritage zone itself, which would especially benefit less-known monuments.

Optimal utilization of space in the heritage zone, bringing in new audiences causing benefits to both the monument’s eyeballs as well as the Haat.

Seamless cultural connection between handicrafts and heritage zones building a multi-sensory journey encompassing architecture, craft and culture.

Ensures neglected parts of a large heritage zone are spruced up and not left to be covered by vegetation or intruded by anti-social elements.

Creates economic opportunities, both to the artisans and to the agency managing the monument. A revenue sharing arrangement could be explored.

Challenges

Process

Curation of such a zone will need to be pioneered by the Union Ministry of Culture, bringing in subject matter experts from the private sector or non-for-profit bodies such as the Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH).

Monitoring the heritage zone to ensure the monument stays untouched is a task for the ASI, of or state department, if it is a state managed monument.

Pan-India model

(The author is a heritage enthusiast)

At the end of August this year, the Prime Minister visited Uzbekistan. Had his visit been a trifle longer and encompassed the Registan complex in Samarkand, he may have come across an interesting feature in the madrasas that constitute the complex. Within each madrasa, the cells where students once lived are now shops for handicrafts, bridging the gap between architectural history and living heritage. The marketplace does not just bring alive the otherwise passive monument, it also creates a ‘heritage zone’ compelling visitors to spend more time and adds to the local economy. This phenomenon of creating heritage zones, common in that country, is something India would do well to learn from.A visitor to the Qutab Minar complex in Delhi, also a UNESCO World Heritage site like the Registan Square, sees a set of magnificent monuments. However, the place gives no clue about the larger heritage ecosystem that lies just beyond the walls of the Qutab complex. And importantly, the opportunity to create a showcase of living heritage too has been missed.Sharing a wall with the Qutab complex is Mehrauli Archaeological Park, dotted with tombs, mosques, a magnificent stepwell, stables, cupolas as well as some British era structures.On the other side of the complex lies Mehrauli village, with more tombs, a dargah, the Zafar Mahal, another stepwell and a tiny World War I marker. Nothing in the Qutab complex indicates the existence of this larger heritage universe.Nor is there any mention of the superb Dastkar Haat, a short drive away. In March this year, the Haat saw a major fire that destroyed over forty shops and caused losses of several crore. To anyone who has visited the place, it is apparent that the Haat suffers from a lack of space. On the other side, the Mehrauli Archaeological Park, spread over 200 acres, lacks publicity and footfalls. The back wall of the park is broken and serves as a thoroughfare for people in Mehrauli village. After dark come the unsavoury elements. An uncovered drain flows through a part of the park. The logical solution would be to marry the two spaces.Imagine a scenario where visitors had an option to exit – or enter - the Qutab complex into the Archaeological Park, in one corner of which the Dastkar Haat is relocated. Currently the park has a solitary café. Create more such cafes and even fine dining areas, as well as an amphitheatre enabling cultural performances and open-air exhibitions.The biggest plus is to create urban spaces in and around hitherto neglected heritage zones that ensure:The Dastkar Haat is a creation of a non-profit society which runs for the welfare of artisans, in partnership with Delhi Tourism. The latter reports to the Delhi State Government while the Delhi Development Authority – which controls the park – is under the Central Government’s Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. The monuments are with the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), under the jurisdiction of the Central Government’s Ministry of Culture. Imagine the sheer number of bureaucrats involved and the resultant turf war. Adding to the confusion are some madrasas, supposedly under the umbrella of the Waqf Board, which are functioning out of monuments.The suggestion of bringing a Haat into the vicinity of a space that has the Jamali-Kamali mosque, Balban’s tomb and the Rajaon-ki-Baoli would instantly anger heritage hardliners, not to mention ASI officials.This model ‘heritage zone’ already exists in Sunder Nursery and begs to be implemented in sites across India. The nursery was once a mere offshoot of the Humayun’s Tomb complex, drawing in only flora and heritage afficionados.Today, it is a magnificent cultural hub.Imagine the Tughlakabad Fort as a place for musical evenings instead of being overgrown with scrub. Imagine if the National Crafts Museum were not in isolation in a corner of Bharat Mandapam but within the Purana Qila complex. Imagine if the neglected spaces near Ujjain’s Kaliyadeh Palace were leveraged to create a crafts bazaar. Imagine if Chhattisgarh’s tribal art, crafts and cuisine were to be given a space – even on a seasonal basis – at the heritage hub of Sirpur. Imagine!
Article Summary: The qutab minar complex in delhi gives no clue about the larger heritage ecosystem that lies just beyond the walls. The dastkar haat, a short drive away, saw a major fire that destroyed over forty shops and caused losses of several crore. This phenomenon of creating heritage zones, common in uzbekistan, is something india would do well to learn from.

Article Title: Delhi HC quashes FSSAI order directing Red Bull to drop 'energy drink' label
Article Text:
The court set said the decision was taken “without affording any opportunity” to the company to present its views.

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Tuesday quashed an order issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) directing Austrian beverage maker Red Bull to stop using the “energy drink” descriptor on its cans.The court set aside the June 30, 2026 order, saying that the regulator had taken the decision “without affording any opportunity” to the company to present its views.The order came after Red Bull challenged the FSSAI directive, which required the company to remove the “energy drink” descriptor from its range of caffeinated beverages.Red Bull had approached the Delhi HC on Monday, challenging the FSSAI order issued by an Assistant Director on June 30. The company said it had been selling its products in India since 2002 using the “energy drink” descriptor.During Monday's hearing, Justice Amit Mahajan sought clarity from FSSAI on whether Red Bull had been issued a show-cause notice and given an opportunity to explain its position before the order was passed.The court also questioned the need for immediate action without first hearing the company and asked FSSAI to take instructions on the matter.No interim protection was granted to Red Bull during Monday’s proceedings.Red Bull also challenged a July 17 communication issued by FSSAI to food safety authorities across states and Union Territories, directing them to take action against allegedly non-compliant products.According to the company’s petition, the June 30 direction was issued without prior notice or an opportunity of hearing. Red Bull further claimed that the July communication led to enforcement action, including the seizure of its products at various locations across the country.The company has questioned the basis for the change in FSSAI’s position, citing a March 2024 advisory which, according to its petition, had clarified that the expression “energy drink” could be used for products falling under the relevant food categories applicable to caffeinated beverages.Earlier in June, India directed makers of high-caffeine beverages sold as “energy drinks” to stop using the description, rejecting efforts to stall the move in a market expected to be worth $1.6 billion by 2028, Reuters reported.Red Bull’s India unit had said the “abrupt prohibition” of the label, without any change to the underlying product standard, “introduces substantial regulatory uncertainty and adversely affects” its existing and planned commercial investments.Energy drinks have faced scrutiny from regulators in several countries over concerns about their high caffeine, sugar and taurine content. England is also set to ban the sale of energy drinks to children under 16 from April next year.
Article Summary: The court set said the decision was taken “without affording any opportunity” to the company to present its views. Red bull had approached the delhi hc on monday, challenging the fssai order issued by an assistant director on june 30. The company said it had been selling its products in india since 2002 using the “energy drink” descriptor.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi backs Gen Z protests: 'Stop punishing women for crimes against them'
Article Text:
"Stop punishing women for the crimes committed against them," Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X.

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday backed the ongoing student-led protests over women’s safety, accusing the government of responding to violence against women by restricting their movement instead of making public spaces safer.His remarks came amid renewed protests in Delhi following the alleged gangrape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park in south Delhi. Hundreds of students, many of them women, have taken to the streets over the past week demanding safer public spaces, stronger policing and greater accountability."Stop punishing women for the crimes committed against them," Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X."Across our country, women are afraid to walk the streets, afraid of being harassed, afraid of being raped. And the government’s answer: stay at home," he said.Rahul Gandhi argued that asking women to restrict their movement amounted to victim-blaming instead of addressing the conditions that make public spaces unsafe."This is patriarchy at work: a system that blames the victim and shields the criminal. It is time to smash it," he said.The Congress leader said the focus should instead be on making streets safer, challenging attitudes that enable violence against women and ensuring swift punishment for offenders."The solution is not to lock women inside. It is to make our streets safe, to confront the mindset of men who mistreat women, and to punish those who attack them, swiftly and without exception," the Congress leader said.Protests over the Aastha Kunj case have grown across Delhi University. Students from institutions including Lady Shri Ram College, Miranda House, Gargi College and BR Ambedkar University have participated in demonstrations, raising concerns over harassment, poorly lit streets and restrictions imposed on women because of safety fears.The issue has also reached the Supreme Court. On Monday, the court questioned the Delhi government and police over recent crimes against women and girls in the national capital and sought accountability over what it described as failures in ensuring public safety.Rahul Gandhi urged more young people, particularly women from Gen Z, to join peaceful protests."Thousands of students and young people are on the streets demanding safety for women. I urge even more young women, especially GenZ across India to come out in stronger numbers," he said."This government is deaf to your pain and will only listen when it’s under pressure. Peaceful protest is your democratic right, and I stand with you wholeheartedly," he added.Creative placards and slogans such as "Abort Patriarchy", "My favourite season is FALL of patriarchy", "Bas bohot ho gaya" (enough is enough), and "Bade bade shehron mein aisi chhoti soch nahi chalegi" (such a narrow mindset will not work in big cities) stood out as protesters marched through the campus amid heavy police presence.
Article Summary: "stop punishing women for the crimes committed against them," rahul gandhi said in a post on x. His remarks came amid renewed protests in delhi following the alleged gangrape of a 17-year-old girl. Hundreds of students, many of them women, have taken to the streets over the past week demanding safer public spaces.

Article Title: 'Excluding Citizens Intentionally': Congress calls ECINet BJP's 'star campaigner' amid SIR row
Article Text:
Congress leader Surjewala questions ECINet over voter roll revision, alleges centralised control

ECI now officially stands for Excluding Citizens Intentionally: Surjewala

21.1% voters missing from Maharashtra draft roll

EC moves to review ECINet system

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Randeep Singh Surjewala on Tuesday alleged that the Election Commission’s centralised ECINet software was restricting the powers of ground-level election officials and could lead to the exclusion of eligible voters during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Surjewala cited the Maharashtra chief electoral officer’s concerns over ECINet and alleged that the system was limiting the ability of Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to independently resolve discrepancies in voter records.The Maharashtra CEO had written to the Election Commission seeking changes to ECINet, including greater discretion for EROs in dealing with logical discrepancies and provisions to ease requirements for certain voters. The request came amid the ongoing SIR exercise in the state.Citing the Indian Express Report, Surjewala also flagged the 21.1% reduction in the number of electors in Maharashtra’s draft electoral roll following the SIR exercise. The draft roll contained around 7.72 crore electors, compared with about 9.79 crore in the previous roll.The reduction does not mean that all these voters have been permanently deleted.Maharashtra election authorities have said the excluded voters can seek inclusion through the claims process, with the reasons for non-inclusion including voters being absent, shifted, dead or duplicate entries.The EC has meanwhile ordered a review of the ECINet system amid concerns over its functioning during the SIR process. A committee headed by a senior deputy election commissioner, with an independent expert has been tasked with examining whether the system complies with the relevant laws and rules.The poll panel has also eased the procedure for voters who receive notices during the SIR process. Under the revised arrangement, Booth Level Officers can visit voters’ homes, collect supporting documents and upload them on ECINet for the ERO to take a final decision, instead of routinely requiring voters to appear in person.
Article Summary: Congress leader surjewala questions ecinet over voter roll revision, alleges centralised control. 21.1% voters missing from maharashtra draft roll following the sir exercise. Ec has meanwhile ordered a review of the ecinet system amid concerns over its functioning.

Article Title: Confession can't be sole ground to convict a person under NSA: SC fines UP govt Rs 10 lakh
Article Text:
Tensions escalated in Sambhal in November 2024 during a court-ordered survey of the Shahi Jama Masjid

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday imposed a cost of Rs 10 lakh on the Uttar Pradesh government, holding that a confession statement by an accused cannot, by itself, form the basis for his detention under the National Security Act (NSA).Uttar Pradesh Police had invoked the NSA against Mulla Afroz in October 2025 over his alleged involvement in the 2024 communal violence in Sambhal.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu delivered the judgment while quashing Afroz’s preventive detention.The NSA empowers the Centre and state governments to detain individuals to prevent them from acting in a manner deemed “prejudicial to the defence of India”. Detention can be ordered for up to 12 months, although it can be revoked earlier.Tensions escalated in Sambhal in November 2024 during a court-ordered survey of the Shahi Jama Masjid, following claims that a Harihar temple had previously stood at the site.On November 24, during the second round of the survey, protesters clashed with security personnel. The violence left four people dead and dozens injured.
Article Summary: Uttar pradesh police had invoked the nsa against mulla afroz in october 2025 over his alleged involvement in the 2024 communal violence in sambhal. The nsa empowers the centre and state governments to detain individuals to prevent them from acting in a manner deemed ‘prejudicial to the defence of india’

Article Title: 288 fugitives brought back since 2019: HM Amit Shah
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Stating that 288 fugitives were brought back by the Modi govt from 36 countries between 2019 and 2026, home minister Amit Shah Monday launched a new extradition portal to synergise and expedite efforts to secure the custody of the other "wanted" criminals hiding abroad, to face justice in India.Delivering the inaugural address at a conference on 'PRAHAAR, counter-terrorism policy and strategy', Shah emphasised govt's "zero-tolerance" approach towards all forms and manifestations of terrorism and advocated institutionalising an automated counter-terrorism response and a result-oriented approach for each pillar and at every level of the PRAHAAR framework.PRAHAAR, unveiled in Feb this year as the country's first anti-terror doctrine, is an acronym for its seven pillars Prevention, Response, Aggregating Internal Capacities, Human Rights, Attenuating conditions for terrorism, Aligning international efforts and Recovery & resilience. It aims at criminalising all terrorist acts and starving terrorists, their financiers and supporters of funding, weapons, safe havens and cyber resources, through collaboration among agencies engaged in intelligence collection and investigation.At the conference attended by secretaries of the ministries of home affairs and external affairs, heads of central police forces, state DGPs, anti-terrorism squad heads of all states/UTs and other cutting-edge police officers the home minister called for consistent efforts to strengthen and improvise PRAHAAR strategy through continuous analysis of terror incidents and establishment of a strong and concrete mechanism for the next 10 years.The home minister asked the anti-terror set-up to focus on the percolation of tenets of PRAHAAR right down to the police station level. He called for coordination among the stakeholders to prevent any delay in action against terrorists and exhorted the states to set up dedicated teams to work in tandem with the central agencies to bring back fugitives.Citing the concerted action taken in the last few months against ISI-backed Shahbaz Bhatti network, Shah said close coordination among agencies at central and state level has resulted in busting of more than 40 modules of the network. "More than 100 FIRs were registered and 350 individuals arrested across 15 states," Shah said, adding govt recently declared the network a terrorist organisation under UAPA.

Shah: close coordination among agencies at central and state level has resulted in busting of more than 40 modules of the shahbaz bhatti network. NEW DELHI:Those were among the last recorded words of Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old Dalit man from Dirba in Sangrur district, before his death. His family alleged that he had been pushed to the edge after questioning Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema about the easy availability of drugs in the area.Gulzar died, but his words reverberated across poll-bound Punjab. The BJP, Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal trained their guns on the Bhagwant Mann government, accusing it of failing to control the drug menace. AAP hit back, questioning their own records in power.Drugs have shadowed election after election in the state. Captain Amarinder Singh went into the 2017 polls promising to break the backbone of the drug trade within four weeks. Five years later, AAP sought votes with its own promise of eliminating the menace within months.Now, with Punjab headed for another assembly election in 2027, drugs are again moving to the centre of the conversation.Only the roles have changed.AAP, which once attacked Congress and the SAD-BJP government from the outside, now has nearly five years in office to defend. Congress wants to use AAP's old promises against it. And the BJP, still trying to expand its footprint in Punjab, has launched perhaps its biggest statewide campaign yet around the issue.Leading the opposition charge is the BJP, which has the weakest presence in the state as of now, but is making the strongest pitch for power.The Punjab BJP, on September 18, launched its 13-day 'Nasha Mukt Yatra' to turn its anti-drug campaign into a statewide political roadshow ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. The party divided its campaign into four yatras covering nearly 4,000 km and all 117 assembly constituencies.The campaign will end on September 30, with Union home minister Amit Shah likely to address the concluding rally. All the top BJP leaders including Union ministers and party chief ministers from other states have joined the campaign against drugs in Punjab.Yet the BJP has a political history to answer for too. For 10 years, from 2007 to 2017, it shared power with the Shiromani Akali Dal, the period AAP repeatedly points to whenever its record on drugs is questioned.Ahead of the 2017 election, Amarinder Singh's four-week promise became one of the defining messages of the Congress campaign. He later clarified that his pledge was about breaking the backbone of the drug supply chain rather than completely eliminating every trace of drugs within a month.By 2022, the roles had changed. AAP was the challenger and Arvind Kejriwal and other party leaders promised quick action, speaking of tackling the menace within three to four months of forming the government.The BJP has done its homework well. It knows that the drug menace in Punjab is deep-rooted and hence has sought a timeframe of two years to eradicate it. However, Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has claimed that the BJP will destroy and eliminate the entire drug network within six months if voted to power in the state.Therein lies Punjab's problem: Congress cannot remind AAP about its three-month promise without being reminded of its own four-week vow. BJP cannot attack AAP without being taken back to its decade in government with SAD.Almost every party pointing fingers today has a past of its own to explain.The Congress narrative on the drug menace seems to have been lost in the face of BJP’s high-decibel anti-drug campaign. The party, which for a long time was struggling to set its own house in order amid infighting, has done little till now to capitalise on the alleged failures of the AAP government to tackle the drug menace.The first big Congress show on the ground was only after Sachin Pilot took charge as state incharge and managed to get the rival state unit factions on one stage to protest against Punjab minister Cheema over the suicide of Gulzar.Pilot said: “If someone raises their voice against drugs, they face such attacks. I believe the government can go to any extent to suppress and conceal these voices. There are two sets of laws in the country, one for ministers and another for the common man. This cannot go on. I feel the government is completely on the back foot regarding the issue of drugs.”He then turned to AAP's pre-2022 promise: “The Aam Aadmi Party had promised in Punjab that they would eliminate the drug menace within three months of forming the government. They stand completely exposed. I sense a stir for change in Punjab, and change will happen.”Leader of opposition Partap Singh Bajwa has blamed both the AAP-led state government and the BJP-led Union government for turning the state's drug crisis into a political blame game instead of dismantling the drug supply chain.“Bhagwant Mann cannot wash his hands of responsibility by talking about cross-border, the BSF and Mundra Port. At the same time, the BJP cannot absolve itself by blaming Punjab while the international border, ports and the national drug-trafficking network fall within areas where the Union government has a critical responsibility. Punjab's youth need action, not a Mann-Modi blame-game,” Bajwa said.The Congress challenge is daunting. While on the one hand it has to target the AAP government’s failures, on the other, it also has to prevent the BJP from running away with the anti-drug fight initiative.SAD faces much the same problem. Bikram Singh Majithia recently took a jibe at the Punjab government when he said: “Under AAP's regime, delivery of drugs is faster than that of food.”Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal has also appealed to women in Punjab to unite and launch an ‘andolan’ to free the state from the drug menace, including through ‘thikri pehra’, a community policing practice in which people guard their localities during emergencies.AAP's response is to ask its rivals to look backwards before judging the Mann government.Punjab minister Cheema, who is at the centre of the row over Gulzar’s suicide, shifted the blame to the BJP and the SAD.“The BJP should look at its own record. The drug menace intensified during the 10 years of the SAD-BJP government from 2007 to 2017. It was during that period that terms such as 'chitta' and 'smack' became widely associated with Punjab, with countless young lives being destroyed by addiction,” Cheema said.Countering the BJP offensive, AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal has alleged that the majority of narcotics entering the country originate from Bharatiya Janata Party-ruled states and major maritime entry points controlled by the Centre.Kejriwal alleged: “Today, 80% of the drugs are coming from BJP-ruled states - Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, UP, Delhi. Has the BJP failed to stop the drug trade in its own states, or does it not want to stop it? Their government has been in power in Gujarat for thirty years, and the highest drug trade is there. Drugs enter India through Mundra Port, and stopping that is the responsibility of the central BJP government.”Bhagwant Mann, meanwhile, has launched the ‘Soorma’ campaign to honour drug-rehabilitated people with specially crafted ‘Soorma’ rings and T-shirts. The chief minister said the initiative aimed to transform recovered drug victims into “Ambassadors of Hope”, who will lead the fight against addiction at the grassroots.The Mann government has numbers with which to defend itself.Punjab Police says its ‘Yudh Nashean Virudh’ campaign has resulted in tens of thousands of cases and arrests. More recent state figures put the tally since March 2025 at 61,824 FIRs, 81,433 arrests and 3,918 kg of heroin seized.AAP presents the numbers as evidence that the state machinery is finally going hard after the networks. Its opponents turn the argument around: if such large quantities are still being seized and so many people are still being arrested, how deeply rooted does the trade remain?High seizures can show a crackdown is working but they can also show the scale of the problem being confronted.The government says its strategy now goes beyond policing. It has expanded treatment and rehabilitation under ‘Yudh Nashean Virudh’, with 547 OOAT centres, 219 de-addiction centres and 91 rehabilitation centres, besides programmes involving schools and local communities.For AAP, this forms the other half of its defence: the battle against drugs cannot be measured only through FIRs and seizures but also through treatment and rehabilitation.In 2017, anger over drugs was directed largely at the SAD-BJP government and Congress promised quick action. By 2022, Congress was on the defensive and AAP used the same issue to argue that Punjab's traditional parties had failed. In 2027, AAP is the incumbent being asked many of the questions it once asked others.The slogans have changed and the roles have reversed, but the question has survived different governments and different deadlines: after so many promises to make Punjab drug-free, why is the state heading into yet another election talking about the same problem?
Article Summary: Drugs have shadowed election after election in the state. The bjp, congress and shiromani akali dal trained their guns on the bhagwant mann government. Aap hit back, questioning their own records in power. Now, with punjab headed for another assembly election in 2027, drugs are again moving to centre of the conversation.

Article Title: To recover fines, link traffic challans to power bills: Supreme Court
Article Text:
SC seeks new way to recover traffic fines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday asked govt to adopt an innovative approach to make traffic law violaters pay fines and suggested challans should be linked with electricity bill to force them to pay the penalty or face power disconnection.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Justice K V Viswanathan also suggested that authorities should take steps for blacklisting vehicles with unpaid challans and also block ownership transfers."It is not just sufficient to keep issuing e-challans. Police may issue thousands and lakhs of such e-challans. Question is recovery of fines as sought to be imposed by way of the e-challans...If people are not paying traffic challans, add it to their electricity dues bill. They'll have to pay electricity bills, otherwise the power line will be disconnected. Work it out. In this country, you have to find a way out," the bench said.The court was informed that challans of Rs 45,000 crore have been issued but Rs 25,000 crore has been recovered so far.It also suggested random checks of vehicles to identify those against which e-challans remained unpaid.
Article Summary: Sc seeks new way to recover traffic fines. Suggests challans should be linked with electricity bill to force them to pay penalty or face power disconnection. Justices j b pardiwala and justice k v viswanathan also suggested that authorities should take steps for blacklisting vehicles with unpaid challans.

Article Title: Will Pakistan decide J&K statehood, asks CM Omar
Article Text:
Jammu & Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: CM Omar Abdullah said Monday that making J&K statehood conditional on the end of militancy would effectively give Pakistan a say in its restoration, as the assembly passed a resolution for full statehood and set off a BJP walkout over its reference to a 2000 autonomy demand.Omar moved the resolution that calls on Union govt to restore full statehood. It refers to the 2000 assembly resolution accepting the state autonomy committee report and seeking greater autonomy, and a 2024 resolution seeking special status and constitutional guarantees for J&K.National Conference, Congress, PDP, Peoples Conference, Awami Ithaad Party and CPM supported it.BJP’s Sunil Sharma called the resolution “anti-constitutional” and “anti-secular”, saying its reference to the 2000 autonomy resolution amounted to seeking restoration of J&K’s “pre-1953 position”. BJP said it supports restoration of statehood but opposes the resolution in its current form. Its legislators entered the well, shouted “Vande Mataram” and “Bharat Mata Ki Jai” and moved a motion against speaker Abdul Rahim Rather.Omar criticised BJP’s opinion that statehood could be restored only after militancy ends. “Then the decision regarding restoration of the statehood will not be taken directly in New Delhi but it will be taken in Islamabad,” he said, adding if Pakistan is blamed for militancy, making restoration conditional on guns falling silent effectively gives Islamabad a say in when J&K gets statehood.“We are not begging,” Omar said. “We rightfully demand that we have the right to a statehood.”Omar said the resolution was rooted in a promise of restoring statehood and had nothing to do with Article 370, 35A or autonomy. J&K lost statehood and was bifurcated into two Union territories, including Ladakh, in Aug 2019 when Centre also scrapped its special constitutional status.The CM said he had deliberately kept Article 370, 35A and special status out of the resolution to prevent BJP from using them to disrupt proceedings. He also criticised NC members who had moved amendments seeking references to Article 370 and 35A, saying they had provided BJP “an excuse to oppose it”.Omar said Supreme Court had directed Centre to restore statehood “at the earliest” after assembly elections in 2024 and questioned whether two years could qualify as “as soon as possible”. Omar said there was still no clarity on when Centre considered the “right time” for restoration.Deputy CM Surinder Choudhary rejected BJP’s position that J&K’s sensitive location justified its UT status, saying nearly half of India’s states share borders with neighbouring countries.
Article Summary: Omar moved the resolution that calls on union govt to restore full statehood. It refers to the 2000 assembly resolution accepting the state autonomy committee report and seeking greater autonomy. National conference, congress, pdp, peoples conference, awami ithaad party and cpm supported it.

Article Title: AAP donor list revealed: Ashutosh Ranka among contributors; check how much Kejriwal gave
Article Text:

How much did Kejriwal give

NEW DELHI: Former AAP spokesperson and now Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Ashutosh Ranka donated Rs 21,100 to the Aam Aadmi Party during 2025-26, before taking up his role in the CJP, according to the party's contribution report filed with the Election Commission.The AAP disclosed Rs 12.10 crore in contributions for 2025-26, a 68% decline from the Rs 38.10 crore it reported in the previous financial year. Punjab AAP president Aman Arora contributed Rs 1.20 lakh through 12 payments of Rs 10,000 each.The latest filing covers the first full financial year after the AAP lost power in Delhi in February 2025. The party continues to govern Punjab, where Trident is based.The AAP had disclosed Rs 11.06 crore in contributions in 2023-24, before the figure rose to Rs 38.10 crore in 2024-25. Prudent was the party's largest donor in 2024-25, contributing Rs 16.40 crore.Among other regional parties, the TDP reported Rs 58.25 crore in contributions for 2025-26, down from Rs 83.03 crore the previous year, while the YSR Congress Party reported Rs 24.31 crore, compared with around Rs 140.04 crore in 2024-25. Article Summary: Ashutosh ranka donated rs 21,100 to the aam aadmi party during 2025-26. Ranka is among the 1,202 numbered entries in the latest donor list. Article Title: AAP donations drop 68%; firm founded by ex-MP who joined BJP had given Rs 5 cr of 12.10 cr

AAP donations drop 68%; firm founded by ex-MP who joined BJP had given Rs 5 crore

How other regional parties fared

NEW DELHI: The Arvind Kejriwal-led Aam Aadmi Party received Rs 12.10 crore in contributions in 2025-26, a 68% drop from the previous financial year, according to its latest report filed with the Election Commission.Nearly 83% of the party's contributions came from two donors, Prudent Electoral Trust and Trident Limited. Both gave Rs 5 crore each. Trident was founded by former AAP Rajya Sabha member Rajinder Gupta.The remaining contributions amounted to around Rs 2.10 crore, according to the report.Gupta was elected to the Rajya Sabha on an AAP ticket in October 2025. Trident's Rs 5-crore cheque was dated January 9, 2026, when Gupta was still with the AAP.He joined the BJP after Raghav Chadha led rebellion, merging two-third of AAP's Rajya Sabha strength into the ruling saffron party in April this year.The AAP had reported contributions of Rs 38.10 crore in 2024-25, compared with Rs 11.06 crore in 2023-24. Prudent Electoral Trust was the party's biggest donor that year, contributing Rs 16.40 crore.The latest filing covers the first full financial year after the AAP lost power in Delhi in February 2025.The party continues to govern Punjab, where Trident is based.The AAP report has 1,202 numbered entries. Punjab AAP president Aman Arora is listed against 12 payments of Rs 10,000 each, adding up to Rs 1.20 lakh.The latest filings of other regional parties also show a decline in contributions compared with 2024-25.The Telugu Desam Party (TDP), which came to power in Andhra Pradesh, reported Rs 58.25 crore in contributions in 2025-26, down from Rs 83.03 crore the previous year. Prudent Electoral Trust was its biggest donor, giving Rs 45 crore, compared with Rs 40 crore in 2024-25.The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which lost power in Andhra Pradesh to the TDP, reported contributions of Rs 24.31 crore. Article Summary: Aap donations drop 68%; firm founded by ex-mp who joined bjp had given rs 5 crore each. How other regional parties fared also show a decline in contributions compared with 2024-25. The telugu desam party (tdp) reported rs 58.25 crore in contributions in 2025-26, down from rs 83.03 crore the previous year.

Article Title: Dhaka begins search for missing Assam woman
Article Text:
The Gauhati High Court

NEW DELHI:

Tribunal declared Assam woman a foreigner, but Gauhati HC set it aside

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bangladesh's home ministry told TOI on Monday that it has launched a search for 43-year-old Assam woman Mumtaz Begum, who was sent to Bangladesh in the intervening night of June 13-14 and has been untraceable since. Top bureaucrats in Dhaka also said they were awaiting official communication from India on the case.Dr Ziauddin Ahmed, additional secretary (Political and Immigration), Bangladesh home ministry, whose office deals with border enforcement, illegal crossings and cross-border deportations, said officials were trying to locate Mumtaz but had no information as of Sunday. The matter was sent to police and other depts late on Sept 27, days after TOI reached out.Gauhati HC on Sept 3 directed MEA to "endeavour to locate Mumtaz in Bangladesh and bring her back". The HC also directed Assam govt to pay her husband Mujammel Hoque Rs 2 lakh interim compensation, observing "she was expelled without her husband or an adult family member being informed". HC found it denied her a chance to challenge it, a violation of democratic due process.Underscoring that basic human rights extend to anyone on Indian soil, the bench directed Assam Police and home dept to "ensure that declared foreign nationals are informed about tribunal orders and that their adult family members are notified before they are moved outside their district".The court criticised the tribunal for stripping her of the "opportunity to challenge the Foreigners Tribunal's opinion before Gauhati HC".With no information in India, TOI contacted journalists, human-rights activists, officials and govt and security establishment sources across Bangladesh, focusing on Sylhet division and adjoining districts, where she could have ended up.A senior Dhaka-based businessman, who wishes to stay anonymous, joined authorities in the search and is working with govt and security contacts. An appeal with her photo and identification details, including Foreigners Identification Portal ID, was published in prominent Bengali newspapers on Sept 22. Bangla daily Manob Kantha also carried her photo and reported on the family's search.Official efforts in Sylhet, however, have found no lead. Sylhet Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sarwar Murshed Shamim said police had "tried to locate Mumtaz within the metropolitan area but had not found her and were continuing the search."Mumtaz, from Nagaon, was declared a foreigner by a Foreigners Tribunal. The HC set aside the opinion and ordered fresh consideration, finding deficiencies in its assessment of evidence including 1965 and 1970 voter-list records of her grandfather, her father's 1977 voter-list record and voter ID, Gaonburah and Gaon Panchayat certificates, a school transfer certificate and land records.She appeared before the tribunal on May 30 with her lawyer, after which police took her into custody. She was taken to Juria and Nagaon Sadar police stations, Matia holding centre in Goalpara, then Eraligool holding centre in Sribhumi (June 4-13).Handed to BSF on June 13, she was sent to Bangladesh on June 14 from Kalaincherra, Cachar, BSF told the HC. Three months on, police, authorities and civil-society members are trying to establish where she is.
Article Summary: Bangladesh's home ministry told toi on monday that it has launched a search for 43-year-old assam woman mumtaz begum. She was sent to bangladesh in the intervening night of june 13-14 and has been untraceable since. Top bureaucrats in dhaka are awaiting official communication from india on the case.

Article Title: Rape cases peaked at 2,199 in 2015, dropped to 1,901 in '25
Article Text: Changes in the law after the Nirbhaya case , which made registration of FIRs mandatory in offences against women, saw rape cases rise from 1,636 in 2013 to 2,166 in 2014 and peak at 2,199 in 2015. Cases fell to 1,699 in 2020 (due to Covid lockdown), the lowest level since 2013 at that point. The number crossed the 2,000-mark again in 2021 and reached 2,141 in 2023. A decline followed, with cases dropping from 2,141 in 2023 to 2,076 in 2024 and further to 1,901 in 2025.
Article Summary: Rape cases rose from 1,636 in 2013 to 2,166 in 2014 and peak at 2,199 in 2015. Cases fell to 1,699 in 2020 (due to covid lockdown), the lowest level since 2013 at that point. The number crossed the 2,000-mark again in 2021 and reached 2,141 in 2023.

Article Title: AAP donations fall 68%, BJD reports zero contributions

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party's receipts from contributions in 2025-26 fell to Rs 12.1 crore, which is less than one-third of its Rs 38.1 crore inflow through this route in 2024-25. Of this, Rs 10 crore, or 83% of its total donations, came from Prudent Electoral Trust and Trident Group founded by Rajya Sabha MP Rajendra Gupta, who switched loyalties from AAP to BJP earlier this year.AAP is the only party that declares all donation receipts and not just those above Rs 20,000 as required by the law. According to its latest contribution report filed with Election Commission (EC), both Prudent and Trident contributed Rs 5 crore each to AAP; in 2024-25, Prudent had donated Rs 16.4 crore to the party.Among regional parties, TDP, which is in office in Andhra Pradesh since 2024, declared its donation receipts at Rs 58.3 crore, though this is less than the Rs 83 crore contributions it had reported the previous year. Prudent contributed over 77% of TDP's total receipts through six donations in 2025-26. In 2024-25 too, Prudent was TDP's biggest donor, having contributed Rs 40 crore in all.YSR Congress Party, the main opposition party in Andhra Pradesh, received a total of Rs 24.3 crore in donations in 2025-26, though this figure is way less than its Rs 140 crore inflow in 2024-25.BRS, which was voted out of office by Congress in Telangana in 2023, declared its total contributions in 2025-26 at Rs 16.4 crore, up from Rs 15.1 crore in 2024-25. The 2025-26 contribution report for Biju Janata Dal (BJD), which was defeated in Odisha in 2024, records nil donations, as against Rs 60 crore declared in 2024-25.Part of AAP's donations in the last fiscal came from its MLAs, including former Delhi CMs Arvind Kejriwal (Rs 30,000) and Atishi Marlena (Rs 42,000).
Article Summary: Aap’s donation inflow falls below one-third to rs 12.1 crore in 2025-26. Of this, rs 10 crore, or 83% of its total donations, came from prudent electoral trust and trident group.

Article Title: High-speed corridors to link UP with North East
Article Text:
Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari​

NEW DELHI: A 630-km corridor connecting Siliguri in West Bengal with Guwahati (Assam) and Shillong (Meghalaya) will be built at a cost of Rs 61,500 crore, announced road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari Monday.The road transport ministry has also taken up an expressway connectivity project from Gorakhpur (UP) to Siliguri.Once completed, the two corridors will provide high-speed connectivity between Uttar Pradesh and North East.Speaking at an event, Gadkari added that the 630-km corridor, which will be the "lifeline" of North East, will have the mix of construction of greenfield (new) stretches and upgradation of existing highway connectivity to make the end-to-end travel seamless. He said the first leg of the corridor, Siliguri to Guwahati (400 km), will be built at an investment of Rs 30,000 crore and the project alignment is in approval stage.
Article Summary: A 630-km corridor connecting siliguri in west bengal with guwahati (assam) and shillong (meghalaya) will be built at a cost of rs 61,500 crore. The road transport ministry has also taken up an expressway connectivity project from gorakhpur (up) tosiliguri.
